Grok Bot alternatives (open source and hosted)

Updated October 31, 2026.

Grok Bot is xAI's hosted product for named bots, a computer they can use, routines, and approvals. The public docs describe a cloud computer on your account. They do not describe installing the service yourself or connecting your own model provider.

Below are alternatives, open source and hosted. WhatEverFi, the open source Grok Bot alternative, is one of them: Apache-2.0 software you can run on your own machine, with a model key you bring.

  • WhatEverFi

    The chat. The roster is the sidebar, and you manage the bot from this conversation.

    Suits someone who wants a persistent bot on a machine they control, with a model key they bring, managed from chat. The license is Apache-2.0. WhatEverFi, the open source Grok Bot alternative.

  • OpenClaw

    Suits someone who wants an MIT-licensed agent on their own machine and will run a Gateway and a config file. OpenClaw comparison.

  • Hermes Agent

    Suits someone who wants Nous Research's MIT-licensed agent, including a desktop app that can reach a first message without the command line. Messaging apps use a separate gateway. Hermes Agent comparison.

  • Meta Muse

    Suits someone who wants Meta's hosted agent in the Muse app or WhatsApp. It runs on a virtual machine Meta operates, and Meta introduced it on September 8, 2026. Meta Muse comparison.

  • OpenAI Dots

    Suits someone on an eligible ChatGPT plan who wants OpenAI's always-on agents. OpenAI announced them on September 29, 2026, and says each dot has its own cloud computer. OpenAI Dots comparison.

  • Instinct

    Suits someone who wants to text or call a hosted assistant. Spear Street Technology, Inc. operates the assistant at instinct.com. Instinct comparison.

  • Hark Pro

    Suits someone who wants the hosted personal agent at hark.com, launched October 6, 2026, with a free tier. $20 a month is twice the usage, and $100 a month is ten times the usage. Hark Pro comparison.

  • Claude Duet

    Suits someone with Claude Pro or Max in the US who wants Anthropic's research-preview agent. It runs on a cloud computer Anthropic operates, and Anthropic released it on October 21, 2026. Claude Duet comparison.

How to choose

Choose an agent you run yourself when the computer and the model key should stay with you. WhatEverFi is Apache-2.0: you host it, you bring the model key, and you manage the bot from chat. OpenClaw is an MIT-licensed agent you run yourself, and its docs add a Gateway and a config file. Hermes Agent is MIT-licensed, with a desktop app that can reach a first message without the command line, and a separate gateway for messaging apps.

Choose a hosted assistant when you do not want to install the service. Grok Bot comes with paid Cursor plans and SuperGrok. Meta Muse runs on a virtual machine Meta operates. OpenAI Dots sit on eligible ChatGPT plans. Instinct is the assistant you text or call. Claude Duet comes with Claude Pro and Max in the US, on a computer Anthropic operates. Hark Pro has a free tier. $20 a month is twice the usage, and $100 a month is ten times the usage.

The alternatives roundup lists license, price, and setup side by side. OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent vs WhatEverFi compares the three you run yourself, and best open source AI agents in 2026 includes libraries as well as apps.

FAQ

Is Grok Bot open source?

Grok Bot, the hosted teammate app, does not publish its source for you to run. xAI has open-sourced other software: Grok Build, the coding-agent CLI, is Apache-2.0, and the older Grok-1 model weights were released under Apache-2.0. Those projects are not the Grok Bot service. WhatEverFi is Apache-2.0, and the application source is public on GitHub.

Can I self-host Grok Bot?

The Grok Bot docs describe a cloud computer assigned to your account. They also describe an optional local computer, where a bot runs approved commands on the machine in front of you. They do not describe installing the Grok Bot service on a server you operate. WhatEverFi can be self-hosted.

How is WhatEverFi different from Grok Bot?

Both are persistent bots that can use a computer, sign in to tools, keep context, and run routines. Grok Bot hosts that computer for you and comes with paid Cursor plans and SuperGrok subscriptions. WhatEverFi is open source: you host it or use WhatEverFi Cloud, in beta, you choose the model, and team computers and private computers stay separate.

Is WhatEverFi just chat, like Grok Bot?

After the install, yes. You create an account, connect a model, and manage the bot from that chat. A new bot interviews you. Routines, memory, and approval boundaries stay with the bot. WhatEverFi is that chat plus the computer you run. Grok Bot is also a chat for named bots. The difference is who hosts the service and who picks the model.

Can I use my Claude Pro/Max or ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription?

Use ChatGPT sign-in with an eligible plan, or connect an API key. For Claude, use an Anthropic API key; Pro and Max subscriptions do not include API credit. See Model subscriptions in the docs for provider restrictions.

What are the other alternatives?

Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct, Claude Duet, and Hark Pro are hosted assistants. OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are open source agents you can run yourself, with a gateway and a config file in their docs. The comparisons page lists licenses, prices, and setup side by side. None of them imports a Grok Bot account.
